blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The Zephyr protocol team, which issues ZYS and ships the mandatory consensus implementation, exercised a holder-facing global control in 2025. HF8 at block 481500 (2025-03-31) disabled ordinary transfers and conversions except mandatory per-holder audit migrations; HF9 at 508000 paused all transactions; HF10 at 511000 reopened only audit migrations. HF11 at 536000 restored ordinary transfers of new assets and permanently invalidated non-migrated ZYIELD and ZEPHUSD balances. Current documentation confirms unaudited assets remain unusable. The demonstrated issuer-driven transfer halt and balance invalidation constitute mutable holder-facing control under possible, despite requiring network adoption of consensus releases. The fUSD precedent differs because its rollback was performed by Zano chain developers rather than the fUSD issuer. Current v2.3.0 commit 67c5f53b878fef41fb5e74c4382d5b7a2f37fd8a retains the historical restrictions behind hardfork-version gates; same-asset ZYS maps to YIELD_TRANSFER, with no standing address blacklist, issuer freeze key or privileged holder burn identified, so true is not established. At official snapshot height 874253, HF11, captured 2026-09-29T07:47:36.883Z, the yield reserve held 328,534.7534294861 ZSD against 165,939.6268199358 ZYS. Its reserve is 100% ZSD, now reviewed possible, giving 100% upstream exposed backing; the direct possible control takes precedence over inherited. No material production wrapper was identified; the discovered EVM bridge remains testnet. Precedents: zsd-zephyr-protocol shares the same demonstrated control; usdk-orki establishes possible for mutable holder-facing control without an active blacklist.

oracleRisk.summary: ZYS mint and redemption prices are consensus-derived from the on-chain ZSD yield-reserve tally and ZYS supply. Yield-reserve accrual converts a ZEPH block-reward allocation into ZSD using Zephyr's signed pricing record; three delivery endpoints share one hard-coded RSA signing key, and nodes may reuse the last acceptable record for up to ten blocks.

branchApplicability.rationale: ZYS is a protocol-wide share of the ZSD Yield Reserve, not a borrower debt market. Its share price is derived from the single yield-reserve tally, while ZEPH-denominated yield accrual uses Zephyr's signed pricing record. There are no collateral-specific liquidation branches, so the complete exposure belongs at top level.
